recipes.recipe_name: Cheesy Chicken and Vegetable Rice Bake
recipes.visual_description: The Cheesy Chicken and Vegetable Rice Bake is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl, showcasing a hearty single portion. Golden-brown chicken chunks, seared to perfection, are nestled amongst fluffy, savory rice. Diced potatoes and vibrant green peas and corn kernels are evenly distributed, adding pops of color and varied textures. Bright green broccoli florets are tender-crisp, peeking through a glistening, melted layer of golden cheddar cheese on top. The cheese has some beautifully browned, bubbly spots. A sprinkle of fresh, finely chopped parsley provides a final touch of verdant freshness. The dish exudes warmth and comfort, with steam subtly rising. It is placed on a simple wooden table with a white linen napkin beside it, under natural, soft lighting.

ingredients.name: medium green chili, deseeded and minced

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Season chicken chunks with salt, pepper, garlic powder, and paprika. Add chicken to skillet. Sear until golden brown on all sides. Remove chicken from skillet.
Add diced onion to skillet. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in rice, diced potato, minced chili (if using), corn, and green peas. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared chicken to the skillet, nestling it into the rice mixture.
Cover skillet with a lid or foil. Transfer to preheated oven. Bake for 20 minutes.
Remove from oven. Stir in broccoli florets.

Sprinkle shredded cheese evenly over the top. Return to oven, uncovered. Bake for another 10-15 minutes, or until rice is tender, liquid is absorbed, and cheese is melted and bubbly. Chicken internal temperature should reach 75°C.
Let rest for 5 minutes before serving. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Poached Chicken Breast, Broccoli Velouté, Thyme Aerated Mayonnaise
recipes.visual_description: A single, perfectly poached chicken breast, pristine white and impeccably smooth, occupies the center of a large, round white bone china plate. Adjacent to the chicken, a small, vibrant green pool of velvety broccoli velouté gleams, reflecting the light. A delicate, airy dollop of pale, off-white thyme aerated mayonnaise rests precisely on the chicken or beside the velouté, its light texture providing visual contrast. The composition is minimalist, with abundant negative space around the elements. One or two tiny, perfectly blanched broccoli florets or micro-thyme leaves are placed with precision as a subtle garnish. The plate rests on a cool, grey-veined Carrara marble surface, illuminated by dramatic professional lighting that creates soft shadows, enhancing the dish's architectural precision. A pristine white linen napkin, folded into a crisp triangle, and a single piece of modern silver flatware complete the ultra-minimalist, sophisticated setting, emphasizing restraint and perfect execution.
instructions: Prepare chicken: Season chicken breasts generously with salt and white pepper. Vacuum-seal each breast individually. Cook in a precise water bath (sous-vide) at 63°C for 1.5 hours. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove from bag, pat dry.

Prepare broccoli velouté: Trim broccoli. Separate florets and stems. Peel stems. Cut stems into 1 cm pieces. Reserve a few tiny florets for garnish. Blanch remaining florets and stem pieces in generously salted boiling water for 5 minutes until very tender. Immediately transfer to an ice bath to stop cooking. Drain thoroughly.

Melt butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Add blanched broccoli. Add chicken stock. Bring to a simmer. Transfer mixture to a high-speed blender. Blend until exceptionally smooth. Pass the velouté through a fine-mesh sieve (tamis) using a spatula for a silky texture. Season with salt, white pepper, and a squeeze of fresh lemon juice. Keep warm.

Prepare thyme aerated mayonnaise: Gently warm neutral oil with fresh thyme sprigs in a small saucepan over low heat for 10 minutes to infuse. Do not fry the thyme. Let oil cool completely. Strain out thyme sprigs. In a small bowl, combine high-quality mayonnaise with the infused thyme oil and a few drops of fresh lemon juice. Using an immersion blender or small whisk, vigorously aerate the mixture just before plating until light and frothy. For a true foam, use a culinary siphon charged with N2O.

To plate: On a large, warm white bone china plate, place one perfectly cooked chicken breast, cut cleanly if desired (e.g., a thick diagonal slice or kept whole). Create a small, elegant pool or artistic swipe of the vibrant green broccoli velouté next to the chicken. Delicately place a dollop or a few small dots of the airy thyme aerated mayonnaise near the chicken. Garnish with one or two tiny, perfectly blanched broccoli florets or a few micro-thyme leaves for visual contrast. Serve immediately.
notes: For best results with the chicken, a sous-vide immersion circulator is highly recommended for precise temperature control and unparalleled tenderness. If unavailable, very gentle poaching in barely simmering chicken stock will also work, ensuring internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Passing the broccoli velouté through a tamis (fine-mesh sieve) is crucial for achieving a truly silky, refined texture.
The aeration of the mayonnaise should be done just before serving to maintain its light, frothy texture. A culinary siphon is ideal for a stable foam.

recipes.recipe_name: Sustainable Prune & Orange Petit Fours
recipes.visual_description: Six to nine perfectly uniform miniature rectangular petit fours are artfully arranged on an unglazed, handcrafted ceramic rectangular platter in a natural cream tone. The petit fours feature a light, golden-hued almond and orange cake base, layered with a deep plum-colored prune and orange preserve. Each delicate bite is topped with a thin, glossy, off-white vanilla glaze, subtly hinting at citrus. A few fine slivers of toasted almond are scattered across the glaze for texture, along with a tiny, delicate curl of candied orange peel, emphasizing zero-waste. The presentation is minimalistic, with ample negative space around the pieces, highlighting their clean lines and natural colors. The platter rests on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface, accompanied by a loosely folded undyed linen napkin. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the scene, emphasizing the pure beauty of the ingredients against a clean, uncluttered background with subtle natural elements.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve elegantly on a shared platter, accompanied by a selection of artisanal teas or freshly brewed coffee, reflecting modern Australian cafe culture.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F). Line a 20x20 cm baking tin with parchment paper.

For the prune and orange preserve: Finely chop prunes. In a small saucepan, combine chopped prunes, 50 ml fresh orange juice, and 2.5 ml vanilla extract. Simmer over low heat for 15-20 minutes. Stir occasionally. Cook until prunes are very soft and liquid reduces to a thick, jam-like consistency. Mash gently. Cool completely.
For the cake: In a large bowl, whisk together almond flour, all-purpose flour, baking powder, salt, and orange zest from the orange. Reserve a few thin strips of orange peel for garnish.
In a separate bowl, whisk together plant milk, remaining 80 ml orange juice, maple syrup, vegetable oil, and 5 ml vanilla extract.
Pour wet ingredients into dry ingredients. Whisk until just combined. Do not overmix.
Pour batter into the prepared baking tin. Spread evenly.
Bake for 20-25 minutes. Cake is done when a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean. Cool completely in the tin on a wire rack.
Once cooled, carefully remove cake from tin. Cut the cake into 6-9 perfectly uniform miniature rectangular pieces.
Split each cake piece horizontally. Spread a thin layer of the cooled prune and orange preserve on the bottom half of each cake piece. Place the top half back on.
For the glaze: In a small bowl, whisk powdered sugar with 20-30 ml fresh orange juice and 2.5 ml vanilla extract until smooth and pourable. Adjust juice for desired consistency.
Drizzle or gently brush glaze over each petit four. Let glaze set slightly.
Garnish each petit four with a few toasted slivered almonds and a tiny curl of reserved candied orange peel. Serve immediately on an elegant platter.
notes: This recipe emphasizes sustainability through minimal processing, use of natural sweeteners, and utilizing ingredients like orange zest and peel to reduce waste.
The prune and orange preserve, slow-cooked to concentrate flavors, highlights a simple form of preservation for enhanced taste.

recipes.recipe_name: Homestyle Curried Cabbage & Tofu Fritters
recipes.visual_description: The Homestyle Curried Cabbage & Tofu Fritters are presented casually on a rustic, round ceramic plate with a slightly uneven rim, placed on a well-used wooden dining table. Three to four golden-brown, irregularly shaped fritters are stacked loosely or arranged naturally, showcasing their crispy, pan-fried exterior and visible flecks of green cabbage, orange carrot, and bright green peas within the soft, savory tofu matrix. The fritters have a comforting, homemade appearance, not perfectly uniform. A small, simple bowl of a light green cilantro-mint chutney or plain yogurt is positioned beside the fritters. The background is slightly blurred, hinting at a cozy kitchen environment with natural, warm light filtering in. A casually folded linen napkin in a muted tone rests nearby. The entire plate is visible, with ample negative space around the food, emphasizing its unpretentious, inviting nature.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of plain yogurt or a simple mint-cilantro chutney.
Enjoy as a hearty snack or light appetizer.
instructions: Press tofu for 30 minutes to remove excess water. Crumble into a large bowl.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add diced onion, grated carrot, and minced garlic. Sauté for 5 minutes until softened.
Stir in Madras curry powder. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add shredded cabbage, diced tomato, and pork stock to the pan. Cover and cook for 5-7 minutes until cabbage is tender-crisp. Stir in green peas. Remove from heat. Let cool slightly.

Add the cooled vegetable mixture to the crumbled tofu. Stir in soy sauce, Dijon mustard, beaten egg, and all-purpose flour. Mix well until all ingredients are combined. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Form the mixture into 8-10 uniform patties, about 2 cm thick.
Heat 2-3 cm vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Fry patties in batches for 3-4 minutes per side, until golden brown and cooked through.
Transfer fried patties to a wire rack lined with paper towels to drain excess oil.
Serve warm.
notes: For best results, ensure tofu is well-pressed to remove excess moisture.
Patties can be made ahead and reheated gently in an oven or air fryer.

recipes.recipe_name: Sustainable Chicken & Chard Pasta with Preserved Tomato
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion of Sustainable Chicken & Chard Pasta with Preserved Tomato is presented on a handcrafted, natural cream-colored ceramic plate, centered on a light bamboo table surface. A whole, pan-seared chicken breast, with a golden-brown crust and moist interior, rests beside a loose, natural mound of short pasta. The pasta is lightly coated in a rustic, slightly chunky sauce made from vibrant red-orange fermented tomatoes. Wide ribbons of deep green swiss chard are gently intertwined with the pasta, adding a pop of color and natural texture. Fresh, vibrant green basil leaves are scattered artfully over the dish, providing a fresh garnish. The composition emphasizes natural forms and textures with ample negative space around the food. The background is minimalist and clean, featuring soft, natural lighting that highlights the dish's organic colors and textures. An undyed linen napkin in a natural beige tone and subtle green plant elements are visible in the soft-focus background, reinforcing the eco-conscious theme.
instructions: For Fermented Tomatoes (prepare 5-7 days in advance): Wash tomatoes. Cut into quarters. Pack tightly into a clean glass jar. Dissolve 15g pickling salt in 500ml non-chlorinated water. Pour brine over tomatoes, ensuring they are fully submerged. Seal jar loosely or use an airlock lid. Ferment at room temperature (18-24°C) for 5-7 days, or until desired tanginess. Refrigerate once fermented.
Prepare Chicken: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with sea salt and black pepper.

Sear Chicken: Heat 15ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add chicken breasts. Sear 6-8 minutes per side until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from pan. Rest on a cutting board, tented with foil.
Cook Pasta: Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Add pasta. Cook according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 120ml pasta cooking water. Drain pasta.
Prepare Swiss Chard: Separate chard leaves from stems. Finely chop stems (for optional stock or discard). Cut chard leaves into wide ribbons (approx. 2-3 cm).

Make Sauce: In the same pan used for chicken, add remaining 15ml olive oil. Add finely diced onion and minced garlic. Sauté 3-4 minutes until softened. Add fermented tomatoes (roughly chopped) and their brine. Break down tomatoes with a spoon. Stir in vegetable stock. Simmer 5-7 minutes, reducing slightly.

Combine: Add drained pasta to the sauce. Add chard ribbons. Toss to combine. If too dry, add reserved pasta water until desired consistency. Cook 2-3 minutes until chard wilts slightly. Stir in half of the fresh basil leaves, roughly torn.
Plate: Divide pasta mixture among four plates. Place one whole pan-seared chicken breast beside the pasta on each plate. Garnish with remaining fresh basil leaves. Serve immediately.
notes: For true zero-waste, use chard stems and tomato scraps to make homemade vegetable stock.

recipes.recipe_name: Sweet Pepper, Pea & Chicken Essence
recipes.visual_description: The dessert is presented on a pristine, matte white ceramic plate with a wide rim, resting on a grey veined marble surface. A single, individual portion of the delicate vanilla bean panna cotta is precisely positioned slightly off-center, its creamy white surface gleaming softly. Beside it, a vibrant, flowing pool of sweet red bell pepper fluid gel cascades elegantly, its rich, glossy texture contrasting with the panna cotta. A precise quenelle of pale green sweet pea mousse is artfully placed atop the panna cotta, offering a delicate, airy counterpoint. Scattered around the base of the panna cotta and the edge of the fluid gel are irregular, golden-brown shards of caramelized chicken skin crumble, providing a unique textural crunch and a subtle, unexpected savory-sweet depth. The composition is minimalist, with abundant negative space highlighting the intentional placement of each component. Natural, dramatic lighting casts soft shadows, enhancing the textures. A polished silver dessert spoon rests beside the plate, and a folded white linen napkin completes the luxurious setting.

ingredients.name: Gelatin sheets (gold grade, for panna cotta)
Gelatin sheet (gold grade, for pea mousse)

instructions: Vanilla Bean Panna Cotta:
Bloom gelatin in cold water.
Combine cream, milk, sugar, vanilla bean and scraped seeds in a saucepan.
Heat gently until sugar dissolves and mixture simmers. Do not boil.
Remove vanilla bean. Squeeze excess water from gelatin. Stir into hot cream mixture until dissolved.
Pour into four small serving molds or glasses. Chill for at least 4 hours until set.
Sweet Red Bell Pepper Fluid Gel:
Preheat oven to 200°C.
Roast whole red bell peppers on a baking tray until skin is charred and blistered.
Place charred peppers in a bowl, cover with cling film. Let steam for 15 minutes.
Peel skin, remove seeds and core.
Blend roasted pepper flesh with water, sugar, and white balsamic vinegar until very smooth. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve.
Pour purée into a saucepan. Whisk in agar-agar powder.
Bring to a boil, simmer for 1 minute, whisking constantly.
Pour into a shallow dish. Chill until set.
Once set, blend the gel again until it becomes a smooth, fluid gel consistency. Store in a squeeze bottle.
Sweet Pea Mousse:
Bloom gelatin in cold water.
Blanch green peas in boiling water for 2 minutes. Drain.
Blend peas with 30 ml water, 20 g sugar, and mint sprig until very smooth. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve.
Gently heat a small portion (approx. 2 tbsp) of pea purée. Squeeze excess water from gelatin. Dissolve gelatin in warm pea purée.
Combine warm pea mixture with remaining cold pea purée. Chill until slightly thickened.
Whip cold heavy cream to soft peaks.
Gently fold whipped cream into the chilled pea mixture until combined.
Transfer to a piping bag. Chill until ready to plate.
Caramelized Chicken Skin Crumble:
Preheat oven to 160°C.
Lay chicken skin flat on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Place another sheet of parchment paper and a second baking sheet on top to press it flat.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until golden brown and very crispy.
Remove from oven. Immediately sprinkle with granulated sugar, pinch of salt, and drizzle with maple syrup.
Return to oven for 5 minutes until sugar caramelizes.
Let cool completely. Once cool, break into small, irregular crumbles.
notes: This dessert pushes boundaries by transforming savory ingredients into a sweet context, focusing on texture, temperature, and sophisticated flavor interplay. The chicken skin provides an unexpected umami and crispy element that balances the sweetness.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Beef Medallions with Garlic-Mustard Sauce
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate centered on a simple wooden table. Two thick, pan-seared beef medallions, perfectly browned with a tender pink interior, are placed slightly overlapping. A rich, golden-brown garlic-mustard sauce is generously spooned over the beef, glistening subtly. Alongside the beef, a cluster of vibrant, blistered roasted cherry tomatoes adds a pop of bright red and a soft texture. A fresh, crisp mixed green salad, tossed with thin slices of red onion and a light vinaigrette, occupies a portion of the plate, providing a contrasting cool green hue. The beef is garnished with a sprinkle of bright green chopped fresh parsley. The composition is balanced and inviting, with appropriate negative space highlighting the quality of the ingredients and precise cooking. Standard silver flatware and a folded white cotton napkin are neatly placed beside the plate.
instructions: Pat beef sirloin medallions dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Preheat oven to 200°C. Toss cherry tomatoes with 1 tbsp olive oil, salt, and pepper on a baking sheet. Roast for 15-20 minutes until blistered.

Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear beef medallions for 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare, or until desired doneness. Transfer beef to a plate, tent with foil, and let rest.
Finely mince garlic and thinly slice half of the red onion. Keep the remaining half of the red onion for the salad.
In the same skillet, add 1 tbsp olive oil. Sauté minced garlic and sliced red onion for 2-3 minutes until fragrant and softened.
Pour in beef broth. Bring to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Stir in Dijon mustard. Reduce heat to medium.
Simmer sauce for 5-7 minutes, or until slightly thickened. Remove from heat. Whisk in butter until melted and sauce is glossy. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
For the salad, combine mixed greens and the remaining thinly sliced red onion in a bowl. Drizzle with balsamic vinegar and 1 tbsp olive oil. Season with salt and pepper. Toss gently.

Plate two beef medallions per person. Spoon generous amounts of garlic-mustard sauce over the beef. Arrange roasted cherry tomatoes alongside the beef. Serve with a portion of fresh green salad on the side. Garnish beef with chopped fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Apple Cider Reduction
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared chicken breast, whole and plump, rests centrally on a clean white round porcelain dinner plate. The chicken boasts a rich golden-brown crust, indicating a perfect sear, and is visibly tender. Thick apple wedges, sautéed until tender with slightly caramelized edges, are arranged neatly beside and around the chicken. A glossy, amber-hued apple cider reduction is generously pooled beneath the chicken and drizzled over the top, adding a reflective sheen. The dish is garnished simply with a few vibrant green fresh thyme sprigs. The plate is positioned on a light, rustic wooden table surface. A neatly folded white cotton napkin and classic silver flatware are placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights the warm tones and textures of the dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of simple roasted potatoes or a fresh green salad with a light vinaigrette.
Offer crusty baguette slices for soaking up the delicious sauce.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Peel, core, and cut apples into 1.5 cm thick wedges. Mince shallots and garlic.
Heat olive oil and 15g butter in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken breasts for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown. Internal temperature must reach 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside to rest.
Add remaining 15g butter to the skillet. Add shallots and sauté until softened, about 2 minutes.
Add garlic and apple wedges. Sauté for 3-4 minutes until apples are slightly tender and caramelized.
If using, carefully add Calvados or brandy to the skillet. Deglaze, scraping up any browned bits. Cook until almost evaporated.
Pour in apple cider and chicken broth. Add two thyme sprigs. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to medium-low.
Simmer sauce for 8-10 minutes, or until reduced by half and slightly thickened. Remove thyme sprigs.
Taste sauce and adjust seasoning. Return chicken to the skillet briefly to warm through in the sauce.
Serve chicken with apple wedges and sauce. Garnish with fresh thyme sprigs.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Resting the chicken after searing helps keep it juicy.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Bell Pepper & Mozzarella Salad
recipes.visual_description: The salad is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. Fresh, dark green rocket leaves form a ruffled bed. Artfully arranged over this are strips of roasted red, yellow, and orange bell peppers, their slightly charred edges visible. Creamy white mozzarella pearls are interspersed, alongside deep red julienned sun-dried tomatoes. Thinly sliced red onion rings are scattered throughout. The composition is lightly drizzled with a golden vinaigrette. A generous scattering of pale, delicate shaved Parmesan curls and vibrant green basil leaves crowns the salad. The plate is moderately filled, with ample negative space. The setting features the plate on a simple light wooden table with a folded white cotton napkin, under soft, natural lighting, creating a professional and inviting atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty ciabatta bread for dipping in the dressing.
Pair with a light Italian white wine, such as Pinot Grigio.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F). Line a baking tray with parchment paper.
Wash and deseed bell peppers. Cut into 2 cm wide strips.
Toss bell pepper strips with 15ml olive oil, a pinch of salt and pepper. Spread on the baking tray.
Roast for 20-25 minutes, or until tender and slightly charred. Let cool.
While peppers cool, prepare dressing. In a small bowl, whisk together remaining 65ml olive oil, red wine vinegar, minced garlic, dried oregano, chili flakes, salt, and black pepper.
In a large bowl, combine cooled roasted bell peppers, drained mozzarella pearls, julienned sun-dried tomatoes, and thinly sliced red onion.
Add rocket to the bowl. Pour dressing over. Gently toss to combine all ingredients.
Divide salad among four plates.
Garnish each plate with fresh basil leaves and shaved Parmesan. Serve immediately.
notes: Bell peppers can be roasted ahead of time and chilled.
Adjust chili flakes to personal spice preference.

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo alla Cacciatora
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pollo alla Cacciatora is presented on a wide, matte white porcelain plate. Two whole, bone-in chicken thighs are stacked slightly in the center, featuring deeply browned, caramelized skin. A thick, rustic sauce covers the base of the plate, filled with visible small cubes of orange carrots, green celery, and translucent onions. Whole, dark purple kalamata olives are nestled within the vibrant red tomato sauce. A light dusting of bright green chopped parsley and a single fresh rosemary sprig garnish the top. Two thick batons of grilled sourdough bread lean against the side of the chicken. The lighting is natural and soft, emphasizing the glossy texture of the braised sauce and the crispness of the chicken skin.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with toasted sourdough bread to soak up the sauce
Accompany with a glass of medium-bodied Italian red wine
Place on a bed of soft, buttery polenta
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a wide braising pan over medium-high heat.
Place chicken skin-side down in the pan.
Sear for 6 minutes until the skin is deep golden and crisp.
Flip chicken and cook for 2 minutes.
Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Add onion, carrot, and celery to the remaining fat.
Sauté vegetables for 8 minutes until softened.
Stir in garlic, rosemary, and sage. Cook for 1 minute.
Pour in red wine. Scrape the bottom of the pan to deglaze.
Simmer wine for 3 minutes until reduced by half.
Add crushed tomatoes and stir to combine.
Place chicken thighs back into the sauce.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 25 minutes.
Check internal temperature of chicken reaches 75°C.
Stir in olives and simmer uncovered for 5 minutes.
Remove rosemary sprigs before serving.
Garnish with chopped parsley.
notes: Always use a meat thermometer to ensure chicken reaches the safe internal temperature of 75°C
Browning the skin thoroughly at the start is essential for the final texture
The sauce should be thick and chunky, not watery

recipes.recipe_name: Pineapple and Ham Stuffed Chicken with Tomato Glaze
recipes.visual_description: A single, plump, golden-brown pan-seared and baked chicken breast, precisely stuffed and presented as a thick medallion, rests centered on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken boasts a rich, slightly crisp exterior, hinting at its tender interior. A vibrant, rustic red tomato glaze, with a subtle sheen, is generously spooned over the chicken and pools elegantly around its base. Small flecks of green fresh thyme leaves are scattered artfully over the chicken and glaze, providing a fresh, aromatic contrast. The plate features moderate negative space, allowing the dish to breathe. The setting is a modern bistro, with a simple light wooden table surface. A neatly folded white cotton napkin and polished silver flatware are placed beside the plate. Natural, soft, even lighting illuminates the dish, emphasizing its inviting textures and colors against a gently blurred, casual restaurant background.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Butterfly each chicken breast. Pound gently to an even 1 cm thickness.
Heat 10ml olive oil in a pan. Sauté diced ham until lightly browned. Add diced pineapple; cook 2 minutes. Remove from heat. Set aside.
Lay pounded chicken breasts flat. Spoon ham and pineapple mixture onto one half of each breast. Fold the other half over. Secure edges with toothpicks.
Season chicken with salt and pepper. Lightly dust both sides with flour.
Heat remaining olive oil and butter in an oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear stuffed chicken 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown.
Transfer skillet to preheated oven. Bake 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C.
While chicken bakes, prepare glaze: In a saucepan, sauté chopped onion in 10ml olive oil until softened. Add minced garlic; cook 1 minute.
Stir in crushed tomatoes and chicken stock. Add 1 sprig of thyme. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cook 10-15 minutes until slightly thickened.
Remove thyme sprig from glaze. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.
Remove chicken from oven. Let rest 5 minutes. Remove toothpicks.
Plate one stuffed chicken breast per serving. Spoon tomato glaze generously over and around chicken. Garnish with fresh thyme leaves.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C for food safety.
Fresh pineapple offers a brighter flavor; canned pineapple should be well-drained.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Red Lentil & Mushroom Hash with Poached Egg and Cheddar
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Spicy Red Lentil & Mushroom Hash is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. A generous, rustic mound of the hash, composed of earthy red lentils, tender sliced mushrooms, and small diced onions, occupies the center. The hash exhibits warm brown and reddish hues with specks of green herbs. Resting perfectly atop the hash is a single, flawlessly poached egg with a creamy white exterior. Golden-orange melted cheddar cheese is draped over parts of the egg and hash, showing a slight bubbling texture. The plate has moderate negative space, allowing the dish to be the focal point. A sprinkle of bright green chopped chives provides a fresh contrast and visual lift. The scene is set on a simple light-toned wooden table surface. Standard silver flatware is neatly placed beside the plate. A folded cotton napkin rests nearby. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and vibrant colors. The background is subtle, suggesting a casual bistro atmosphere.
instructions: Rinse red lentils. Combine lentils and 500 ml vegetable broth in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat. Simmer for 15-20 minutes until tender. Drain any excess liquid. Season with salt and pepper.
While lentils cook, prepare vegetables. Dice onions into small cubes. Thinly slice mushrooms. Mince garlic.

Heat olive oil and butter in a large sauté pan over medium-high heat. Add diced onions. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened and translucent. Add sliced mushrooms. Cook for 8-10 minutes until mushrooms release their liquid and brown. Stir in minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.

Add cooked lentils to the mushroom and onion mixture. Stir in remaining 250 ml vegetable broth and 30 ml hot sauce. Cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until liquid is absorbed and hash is well combined. Season with salt and pepper to taste.

Fill a wide, shallow pot with water. Add white vinegar. Bring to a gentle simmer. Crack each egg into a small bowl. Carefully slide each egg into the simmering water. Poach for 3-4 minutes until whites are set and yolks are still runny. Remove eggs with a slotted spoon. Drain excess water.

Preheat oven broiler. Spoon individual portions of hot lentil hash onto oven-safe plates or into small gratin dishes. Place one poached egg on top of each portion of hash. Sprinkle grated cheddar cheese over the egg and hash.
Broil for 1-2 minutes, watching carefully, until cheese is melted and bubbly. Remove from oven.
Garnish each plate with chopped fresh chives or parsley. Drizzle remaining hot sauce over the hash, if desired. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Coq au Bière with Garlic Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single, robust portion of Coq au Bière is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, set on a simple wooden table surface in a modern bistro setting. A single, golden-brown seared chicken thigh sits prominently, bathed in a rich, dark amber sauce with visible chunks of braised carrots, celery, and halved cremini mushrooms. The sauce has a glossy, thick texture. Beside the chicken, a neat mound of fluffy, white garlic rice provides a bright contrast. The chicken skin is slightly crisp, while the meat appears tender and falling off the bone. A scattering of vibrant green chopped fresh parsley garnishes the dish, adding a pop of color. The composition is balanced, with moderate negative space. A cotton napkin and standard flatware are placed beside the plate. The scene is illuminated by natural, even lighting, creating a warm and inviting atmosphere. The overall presentation is professional and approachable.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty baguette to sop up the rich sauce.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.

Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat. Sear chicken skin-side down until golden brown and crispy, about 5-7 minutes. Flip and sear other side for 3 minutes. Remove chicken. Set aside.
Add lardons to the pot. Cook until crispy, about 5-7 minutes. Remove lardons with a slotted spoon. Reserve rendered fat.
Add diced onion, sliced carrots, and sliced celery to the pot. Sauté in bacon fat until softened, about 8-10 minutes.
Add minced garlic and halved mushrooms. Cook for 3-5 minutes until mushrooms soften.
Sprinkle flour over vegetables. Stir constantly for 1 minute.
Pour in Belgian ale and chicken stock. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer.
Return chicken to the pot. Add thyme sprigs and bay leaf. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 45-60 minutes, or until chicken is very tender and reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
While chicken braises, prepare garlic rice. Rinse rice under cold water until clear. Drain well.
In a medium saucepan, melt butter with 1 tablespoon olive oil over medium heat. Add 2 minced garlic cloves. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add rinsed rice to the saucepan. Stir to coat. Add 600 ml water and a pinch of salt. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 15-18 minutes, or until water is absorbed and rice is tender. Remove from heat. Let stand covered for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork.
Once chicken is cooked, remove chicken, thyme, and bay leaf from the pot. Increase heat to medium-high. Simmer sauce, stirring occasionally, until slightly thickened, about 5-10 minutes.
Return cooked lardons to the sauce. Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Serve braised chicken with a generous portion of garlic rice. Spoon rich sauce and vegetables over chicken. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Cheddar Egg Rice Bowl
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented in a deep, clean white porcelain bowl, centered on a simple wooden table. Fluffy white long-grain rice forms the base, generously topped with bright yellow, melting grated sharp cheddar cheese. A perfectly fried egg, with a vibrant orange-yellow runny yolk and crisp white edges, rests prominently on the cheese. Around the egg, a scattering of golden-brown, crispy caramelized onion strands adds texture. Irregularly shaped, golden-brown garlic bread croutons are interspersed, offering crunchy contrast. A bold zig-zag of bright red hot sauce visually connects the elements, providing a dynamic color pop. Freshly chopped green chives are lightly sprinkled over, adding a final touch of freshness. The scene is lit with natural, even light, with a cotton napkin beside the bowl.

ingredients.name: Day-old bread (sourdough or rustic loaf)
ingredients.quantity: 2 thick slices, cut into 1.5 cm cubes

ingredients.name: Fresh chives or spring onion greens

instructions: Rinse rice thoroughly. Combine 250 g rice with 500 ml water in a saucepan. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until water is absorbed. Let stand covered for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork.

Heat 15 ml olive oil and 15 g butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Add thinly sliced onion. Sauté, stirring occasionally, for 10-12 minutes until deeply caramelized and crispy. Remove from skillet and set aside.

In the same skillet, add remaining 15 ml olive oil and 15 g butter. Add bread cubes and minced garlic. Toast over medium heat, stirring frequently, for 5-7 minutes until golden brown and crispy. Season with a pinch of salt. Remove from skillet.
Heat a non-stick pan over medium heat. Add a small amount of oil if needed. Crack eggs into the pan. Fry eggs to your desired doneness, preferably with a runny yolk. Season with salt and pepper.
Divide cooked rice among 4 individual serving bowls. Top each rice portion with a generous amount of grated cheddar cheese. The warmth of the rice will start to melt the cheese.
Place one fried egg on top of the cheese in each bowl. Arrange a portion of crispy onions and garlic croutons around the egg.
Drizzle hot sauce generously over the egg and cheese. Garnish with fresh chopped chives or spring onion greens. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Crab, Potato, and Butternut Squash Gratin
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous rectangular portion of a baked gratin rests centrally on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The gratin features a golden-brown, bubbling crust of melted cheddar cheese on top, with slight charring at the edges indicating crispy texture. Beneath the crust, layers of thinly sliced, tender light-yellow potatoes and pale orange butternut squash are visible, interspersed with creamy white cheese sauce and delicate chunks of white crab meat. The potatoes and squash maintain their thinly sliced, slightly overlapping shapes, providing a subtle textural pattern. A few small, bright green fresh thyme leaves are scattered artfully over the gratin's surface, adding a pop of color and freshness. The plate is positioned on a simple wooden table surface, suggesting a modern bistro setting. To the left, a neatly folded light grey cotton napkin and a set of polished silver flatware (fork and knife) are arranged. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its warmth and rich textures, with a soft, inviting background blur of a restaurant interior. The entire plate is visible, with moderate negative space around the gratin, creating a professional yet approachable presentation.

ingredients.name: Butternut squash
ingredients.quantity: 500g, peeled, deseeded, and thinly sliced (2-3mm thick)

instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F). Lightly grease a 2.5-liter gratin dish.
In a large saucepan, melt butter over medium heat. Add diced onion. Cook until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes.
Stir in flour. Cook for 1-2 minutes, stirring constantly, to form a roux.
Gradually whisk in dark beer, then verjus, until smooth. Slowly add milk, whisking continuously to prevent lumps.
Bring the sauce to a gentle simmer, stirring, until it thickens. Remove from heat.
Stir in 150g of grated cheddar cheese and the hot sauce until cheese is melted and sauce is smooth. Season with salt and pepper.
Arrange half of the thinly sliced potatoes in an even layer in the prepared gratin dish. Top with half of the butternut squash slices.
Distribute half of the lump crab meat evenly over the squash.
Ladle half of the cheese sauce over the layers.
Repeat with the remaining potatoes, squash, crab, and cheese sauce.
Sprinkle the remaining 50g of grated cheddar cheese over the top.
Bake for 50-60 minutes, or until potatoes and squash are tender and the top is golden brown and bubbling.
Let the gratin rest for 10 minutes before serving. Garnish with fresh thyme leaves if desired.
notes: The verjus provides a subtle tang that brightens the rich cheese sauce.
Adjust hot sauce to desired spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Cheesy Chickpea & Ramen Noodle Stir-Fry with Soft Egg
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Cheesy Chickpea & Ramen Noodle Stir-Fry is presented in a clean white porcelain bowl. Golden ramen noodles form the base, tossed with vibrant julienned red and yellow bell peppers, thinly sliced onions, and creamy green chickpeas. The stir-fry is coated in a glossy, savory sauce. Two soft-boiled egg halves, revealing their rich, jammy yolks, are carefully placed on top. A sprinkle of thinly sliced green onions and white sesame seeds adds a fresh, aromatic garnish. The composition is balanced, allowing for moderate negative space around the well-proportioned ingredients. The dish sits on a simple wooden table surface in a modern bistro setting. A cotton napkin and a pair of chopsticks rest beside the bowl. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, highlighting the textures and colors of the dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately while hot.
Offer additional soy sauce or chili crisp on the side for custom seasoning.

ingredients.name: Ramen noodles (instant ramen blocks without seasoning packets)

instructions: Boil water in a medium saucepan. Gently lower eggs into boiling water. Cook for 6-7 minutes for soft-boiled eggs. Immediately transfer eggs to an ice bath. Peel once cool. Halve each egg lengthwise.
Cook ramen noodles according to package directions until tender. Drain well. Set aside.
Whisk together soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, and brown sugar in a small bowl. Set aside.
Heat vegetable oil in a large wok or deep skillet over medium-high heat.
Add sliced onion and bell peppers. Stir-fry for 3-4 minutes until tender-crisp.
Add minced garlic and grated ginger. Stir-fry for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add drained chickpeas to the wok. Stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Add cooked ramen noodles to the wok. Pour in the prepared sauce. Toss well to coat all ingredients.
Reduce heat to low. Add shredded cheddar cheese. Stir gently until cheese melts and coats the noodles and vegetables.
Divide the noodle mixture among four serving bowls. Top each serving with two soft-boiled egg halves. Garnish with sliced green onions and sesame seeds. Serve immediately.
notes: Adjust brown sugar to taste for desired sweetness.
For extra spice, add a pinch of chili flakes to the sauce.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Creamy Polenta and Parmesan Crisp
recipes.visual_description: A single, elegant starter portion is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. A creamy, golden-yellow mound of smooth polenta forms the base, its surface glistening. Beside it, two perfectly seared chicken medallions, with a deep golden-brown crust, are arranged neatly. The chicken pieces are whole, not sliced. Minced garlic bits are visible on the chicken. A delicate, golden-brown Parmesan crisp stands vertically within the polenta, adding textural contrast. Finely chopped fresh parsley lightly scatters over the chicken and polenta. The dish has moderate negative space, showcasing a professional, approachable composition. The setting is a modern bistro, with a simple wooden table and a cotton napkin beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its inviting colors and textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty Italian bread.
Offer a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and lemon as a light accompaniment.

ingredients.name: Chicken breast
ingredients.quantity: 400g (2 boneless, skinless breasts), cut into 8 medallions

instructions: Prepare Parmesan crisps: Preheat oven to 180°C. Line a baking tray with parchment paper. Spoon 50g grated Parmesan into four 8cm circles, leaving space between them. Bake for 5-7 minutes, until golden and crisp. Remove and let cool on the parchment paper.

Cook polenta: Bring chicken broth to a boil in a medium saucepan. Slowly whisk in polenta, stirring constantly to prevent lumps. Reduce heat to low. Cook, stirring frequently, for 5-7 minutes, until polenta is thick and creamy.
Finish polenta: Remove polenta from heat. Stir in 50g grated Parmesan and 15g butter. Season with salt and pepper. Cover to keep warm.
Sear chicken: Pat chicken medallions dry. Season with salt and pepper. Heat olive oil and remaining 15g butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add minced garlic to the skillet. Cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add chicken medallions to the skillet. Sear for 3-4 minutes per side, until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C).
Plate: Spoon a generous portion of creamy polenta onto the center of each white porcelain plate. Arrange two seared chicken medallions beside the polenta.
Garnish: Place one Parmesan crisp upright into the polenta. Sprinkle chopped fresh parsley over the chicken and polenta. Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure polenta is stirred frequently to prevent sticking and achieve a smooth consistency.
Adjust cooking time for chicken based on thickness; ensure it is cooked through but not dry.
traditional_techniques: Mantecare (for polenta, incorporating fat and cheese for creaminess)

recipes.recipe_name: Zero-Waste Thai Sausage & Spinach Soup
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of clear Thai soup is presented in a deep, handcrafted ceramic bowl with a rustic, unglazed exterior in natural beige. The transparent, golden-amber broth forms the base, revealing crumbled, browned Italian sausage chunks and tender, thinly sliced mushrooms at the bottom. Vibrant green spinach leaves, gently wilted, float elegantly on the surface. A small scoop of fluffy white jasmine rice is nestled on one side of the bowl. The soup is artfully garnished with a swirl of reddish Quick Fermented Chili-Garlic Relish, a scattering of golden-crisp fried garlic bits, and fresh green cilantro leaves. The bowl sits on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface, accompanied by a pair of natural wood chopsticks resting on a small ceramic rest. A folded undyed linen napkin in beige is placed beside the bowl. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene, highlighting the dish's fresh colors and textures against a clean, minimalist background with subtle green plant elements.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with additional lime wedges on the side for personal adjustment of sourness.
Offer a small dish of fish sauce with sliced bird's eye chilies for extra spice and umami.
Serve alongside a simple plate of sticky rice or additional jasmine rice.
instructions: Prepare zero-waste broth: Combine mushroom stems, spinach stems, and clean garlic skins with 1.5 litres of water. Simmer for 30 minutes. Strain broth. Discard solids.
Cook jasmine rice: Rinse rice thoroughly. Cook according to package directions. Set aside.
Make Quick Fermented Chili-Garlic Relish: Finely mince 3 garlic cloves and red chilies. Combine with a pinch of salt. Let sit at room temperature for 1-2 hours. Stir in a teaspoon of lime juice.

Prepare Italian sausage: Remove sausage from casings. Crumble meat. Heat vegetable oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Add crumbled sausage. Cook until browned and cooked through, about 8-10 minutes. Break up any large pieces. Drain excess fat. Remove sausage from pot. Set aside.

Sauté aromatics: Add remaining 3 minced garlic cloves to the same pot. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant. Bruise lemongrass stalks with the back of a knife. Add bruised lemongrass, sliced galangal, and kaffir lime leaves to the pot. Sauté for 2 minutes.
Build soup base: Pour strained zero-waste broth into the pot. Bring to a simmer. Add fish sauce, lime juice, and palm sugar. Stir until sugar dissolves. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Add mushrooms and sausage: Slice mushroom caps thinly. Add sliced mushrooms to the simmering broth. Cook for 3-4 minutes until tender. Return cooked Italian sausage to the pot. Heat through.
Add spinach: Add fresh spinach leaves to the soup. Cook for 1-2 minutes until wilted.

Serve: Ladle hot soup into individual bowls. Add a scoop of cooked jasmine rice to each bowl. Top with cooked sausage, mushrooms, and spinach. Garnish with fresh cilantro and a spoonful of Quick Fermented Chili-Garlic Relish. Serve immediately.
notes: The 'Quick Fermented Chili-Garlic Relish' provides a tangy, spicy kick and utilizes a simple preservation technique. For a deeper fermented flavor, prepare it 1-2 days in advance.
To maximize zero-waste, save vegetable scraps from other meals for the broth base.
traditional_techniques: Balancing sweet, sour, salty, and spicy flavors
Infusing broth with fresh aromatics (lemongrass, galangal, kaffir lime leaves)
Using a clear, light broth base (Gaeng Jued style)

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Chicken Thighs with Umami Potato Puree and Tomato Confit
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion is presented on a handcrafted, off-white ceramic plate with a matte finish, resting on a light, reclaimed wood surface. A generous, organic mound of creamy potato puree forms the base, its natural texture visible. Nestled beside it is a perfectly roasted chicken thigh, skin-on and bone-in, displaying a rich, golden-brown crispness. Scattered around the plate are clusters of deeply seared mixed mushrooms, their earthy browns and varied shapes adding natural contrast. Bright bursts of rich red tomato confit, some slightly shriveled and glistening, are artfully placed, along with soft roasted garlic cloves. The dish is garnished simply with a few vibrant green fresh thyme leaves, enhancing the natural color palette. The composition is clean and unforced, with ample white space, highlighting each ingredient's inherent beauty. Soft natural lighting illuminates the scene.
instructions: Prepare Mushroom Broth: Place reserved mushroom stems in a small saucepan. Add 100ml vegetable stock or water. Simmer gently for 15 minutes. Strain, reserving the concentrated broth. Discard solids or compost.

Make Tomato Confit: Preheat oven to 160°C. In a small oven-safe dish, combine halved cherry tomatoes, 2 peeled garlic cloves, 2 sprigs thyme, and 30ml olive oil. Season lightly with salt and pepper. Roast for 30-40 minutes, or until tomatoes are soft and slightly shriveled.

Roast Chicken Thighs: Increase oven temperature to 200°C. Pat chicken thighs dry. Rub with 20ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Place skin-side up on a baking sheet. Roast for 30-35 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C and skin is crispy. Rest for 5 minutes.

Prepare Potato Puree: While chicken roasts, boil potato chunks in salted water until very tender, about 15-20 minutes. Drain well. Mash potatoes with remaining 30ml olive oil, remaining 2 peeled garlic cloves (or fermented garlic if using), and the mushroom broth. Season with salt and pepper. Mash until smooth or slightly rustic, depending on preference.

Sear Mushrooms: Heat a large pan over medium-high heat. Add a splash of olive oil. Add sliced mushroom caps and remaining sprigs of thyme and rosemary. Sear until golden brown and tender, about 5-7 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.

Plate: Spoon a generous portion of potato puree onto each plate, creating a natural, organic shape. Place one roasted chicken thigh beside the puree. Arrange a small pile of seared mushrooms next to the chicken. Scatter tomato confit and roasted garlic cloves around the plate. Garnish with a few fresh thyme leaves.
notes: For enhanced flavor and probiotic benefits, consider using lacto-fermented garlic in the potato puree. If not available, fresh garlic works well.
Save chicken bones for making nutritious chicken stock, contributing to a zero-waste kitchen.
Mushroom stems can also be dried and ground into a 'mushroom dust' for an umami seasoning.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken Breast, Saffron Risotto, Roasted Red Pepper Coulis, Wild Mushroom Medley
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared chicken breast, its skin golden and crisp, rests elegantly on an expensive bone china plate with a subtle, modern pattern. Beside it, a generous, fluid quenelle of vibrant saffron risotto, its golden hue contrasting with the creamy white of the chicken. A streak of vivid, smooth roasted red pepper coulis sweeps across the plate, providing a bold splash of color. Artfully arranged clusters of sautéed wild mushrooms and tender confit garlic cloves are nestled near the chicken. The plate features abundant negative space, highlighting each component's pristine presentation. A few delicate microgreens provide a final touch of fresh color. The scene is set on a polished dark wood table under dramatic professional lighting, casting soft shadows. A pristine white linen napkin, folded into a precise triangle, complements the minimalist background.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Halve red bell peppers. Remove seeds. Place cut-side down on a baking tray. Roast for 25-30 minutes until skin blackens. Transfer to a bowl. Cover tightly with cling film. Let cool 15 minutes. Peel off skin. Discard skin. Blend roasted pepper flesh with 2 tablespoons olive oil and a pinch of salt until very smooth. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve for a silky coulis. Set aside.

For garlic confit, peel 4 garlic cloves. Place in a small saucepan. Cover with 30ml olive oil. Simmer over very low heat for 20-25 minutes until tender and golden. Do not brown. Remove garlic from oil. Set aside.

For saffron risotto, bloom saffron in 50ml hot chicken stock for 10 minutes. In a large saucepan, heat 1 tablespoon olive oil. Add diced shallot. Sauté until translucent, about 3 minutes. Add rice. Toast for 2 minutes, stirring constantly. Deglaze with white wine. Cook until wine evaporates. Add saffron-infused stock. Stir. Begin adding remaining hot chicken stock, one ladle at a time. Stir constantly. Wait until liquid is almost absorbed before adding next ladle. Continue for 18-20 minutes until rice is al dente and creamy. Stir in grated Parmesan and cold butter. Season with salt and pepper. Risotto should be fluid, not stiff.

Pat chicken breasts dry. Season skin generously with salt and pepper. Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in an oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Place chicken skin-side down. Sear for 6-8 minutes until skin is deeply golden and crispy. Flip chicken. Add remaining 2 whole garlic cloves and 2 thyme sprigs to skillet. Transfer skillet to preheated 200°C oven. Roast for 10-12 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Rest chicken on a cutting board for 5 minutes before serving.

While chicken rests, clean mushrooms. Slice larger mushrooms. Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a separate pan over medium-high heat. Add mushrooms. Sauté until golden and tender, about 5-7 minutes. Season with salt and pepper. Add confit garlic cloves to mushrooms in final minute of cooking.

To plate, create a generous swoop of saffron risotto on one side of a large, shallow plate. Place one rested chicken breast on the plate, slightly overlapping the risotto. Arrange sautéed wild mushrooms and confit garlic artfully beside the chicken. Drizzle or create a delicate streak of roasted red pepper coulis across the plate. Garnish with a few microgreens.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken and Mushroom Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of creamy, free-flowing risotto is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The risotto is a warm, pale yellow hue, studded with tender, golden-brown seared chicken cubes (2cm) and sautéed earthy brown mushroom slices. Finely diced onion pieces are visible throughout the creamy rice. A vibrant sprinkle of fresh green chopped parsley garnishes the top, alongside delicate shavings of Parmesan cheese. The dish has a natural, organic arrangement, showcasing its rich texture. The plate is set on a simple wooden table, with classic silver Italian flatware (fork and spoon) placed beside it, and a folded cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish, with a softly blurred modern bistro background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread.
Pair with a light Italian white wine.
instructions: Dice chicken breast into 2cm cubes. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large pot or deep pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken cubes until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken and set aside.
Add remaining 15ml olive oil and 15g butter to the same pot.
Sauté finely diced onion until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and sliced mushrooms. Cook until mushrooms are tender and browned, about 5-7 minutes.
Stir in Arborio rice. Toast rice for 2 minutes, ensuring all grains are coated.
Pour in white wine. Stir constantly until wine is fully absorbed.
Add one ladleful (about 250ml) of hot chicken broth. Stir continuously until liquid is absorbed.
Continue adding broth, one ladleful at a time. Stir constantly and wait for each addition to be absorbed before adding the next. This process takes about 20-25 minutes.
When rice is creamy and al dente, stir in cooked chicken.
Remove from heat. Stir in remaining 15g butter and grated Parmesan cheese.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve immediately. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and extra shaved Parmesan.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Coriander Masala
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant Chicken and Coriander Masala is presented in a deep white porcelain bowl, showcasing rich, reddish-brown chicken chunks generously coated in a thick, aromatic, subtly textured gravy. The chicken pieces, cut into 4 cm chunks, are tender and retain their shape. The sauce is flecked with finely diced onions and vibrant green specks of fresh coriander. A generous sprinkle of bright green fresh coriander leaves garnishes the top, adding a burst of color and freshness. The bowl is placed on a simple wooden table. Beside it, a small, perfectly mounded portion of fluffy white basmati rice sits in a smaller white bowl, and a piece of warm, slightly blistered naan bread is folded neatly. The setting is a modern bistro style with natural, even lighting, creating a warm and inviting atmosphere. The entire plate is visible, with moderate negative space, highlighting the dish as the centerpiece.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm naan bread or roti
Serve with fluffy basmati rice
Offer a side of cooling raita (yogurt dip) or pickled vegetables (achar)
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add sliced onions. Sauté until deeply golden brown and caramelized, about 10-15 minutes.
Add grated ginger and minced garlic. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in turmeric, cumin, ground coriander, and red chili powder (if using). Cook for 30 seconds, stirring constantly.
Add chicken chunks. Sear chicken on all sides until lightly browned.
Pour in chopped tomatoes and water or chicken stock. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and cook for 20-25 minutes, or until chicken is cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Stir occasionally.
Stir in yogurt and garam masala. Cook for 5 minutes, uncovered, until sauce thickens slightly.
Stir in most of the fresh chopped coriander. Season with salt to taste.
Serve hot, garnished with remaining fresh coriander.
notes: For a richer curry, brown chicken well before adding other ingredients.
Adjust chili powder to your preferred spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Pesce alla Puttanesca
recipes.visual_description: An individual portion of Pesce alla Puttanesca is presented in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. A thick, flaky white fish fillet, such as cod or snapper, is gently poached and nestled in a vibrant, rustic red tomato sauce. The sauce is rich and fluid, generously studded with dark, whole Kalamata olives and bright green capers. Small flecks of red chili flakes are visible throughout the sauce, adding a subtle visual warmth. The dish is garnished with a generous scattering of roughly chopped fresh flat-leaf parsley, providing a contrasting pop of green and a fresh aroma. The overall composition is natural and inviting, with moderate negative space. The bowl sits on a simple light wooden table. A folded white cotton napkin and a piece of crusty artisan bread are placed beside the bowl, completing a casual yet refined Italian dining experience under natural, even lighting.

ingredients.name: White fish fillets (e.g., cod, snapper, halibut)

instructions: Pat fish fillets dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, deep pan or pot over medium heat.
Add minced garlic and red chili flakes. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant. Do not brown garlic.
Pour in crushed tomatoes. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Add pitted olives and rinsed capers to the sauce. Stir well.
Reduce heat to low. Gently place fish fillets into the simmering sauce. Ensure fish is mostly submerged.
Cover the pan. Cook for 8-12 minutes, or until fish is opaque and flakes easily with a fork. Cooking time depends on fish thickness.
Remove pan from heat. Gently transfer each fish fillet and a generous portion of sauce to individual plates or shallow bowls.
Garnish generously with fresh, roughly chopped parsley. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Swordfish with Cherry Tomato and Chili Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single, thick pan-seared swordfish steak, golden-brown and slightly caramelized, rests centrally on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The swordfish is presented as a whole piece, not sliced. It is generously covered with a vibrant, rustic sauce of burst and whole cherry tomatoes, appearing glossy and bright red. Thin slices of garlic and flecks of red chili are visible within the sauce, along with dark green capers. A generous scattering of fresh, bright green chopped flat-leaf parsley provides a fresh contrast. The dish exhibits a natural, organic arrangement with the sauce pooling slightly around the fish. The plate sits on a simple light wooden table surface, accompanied by standard silver flatware and a folded white cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors against a soft, unobtrusive restaurant-style background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to absorb the flavorful sauce.
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and lemon.
Enjoy with a glass of dry white wine, such as Vermentino or Pinot Grigio.

ingredients.name: Red chili flakes
ingredients.quantity: 5g, or 1 fresh red chili, thinly sliced

instructions: Pat swordfish steaks dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat 30ml olive oil in a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat.
Sear swordfish steaks for 3-4 minutes per side until cooked through and flaky. Remove from pan. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add remaining 30ml olive oil to the same pan.
Add sliced garlic and chili flakes (or fresh chili). Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant. Do not brown garlic.
Add cherry tomatoes to the pan. Cook for 5-7 minutes, pressing gently to burst some tomatoes.
Stir in capers and white wine. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 2-3 minutes until wine slightly reduces.
Return swordfish to the pan. Spoon sauce over fish. Heat gently for 1 minute.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Tomato, Cucumber, and Feta Salad with Grilled Chicken
recipes.visual_description: The salad is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, mounded centrally with natural, organic arrangement. Vibrant red diced tomatoes, bright green diced cucumbers, thinly sliced purple red onion, dark Kalamata olives, and creamy white crumbled feta cheese create a rich color palette. Small, golden-brown diced chicken pieces are interspersed throughout the vegetables, showing their seared exterior. Fresh green basil and oregano leaves are scattered generously over the top, adding a final pop of color and texture. A light sheen of olive oil vinaigrette coats the ingredients. The setting is a simple wooden table with a white cotton napkin and standard flatware, embodying a modern bistro aesthetic. The lighting is natural and even, highlighting the fresh ingredients.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm pita bread or crusty artisanal bread for dipping into the flavorful dressing.
Often accompanied by additional olives or a small bowl of hummus.
instructions: Pat chicken breast dry. Dice into 2 cm cubes. Season with 1 clove minced garlic, 5 ml olive oil, 5 g chopped fresh oregano, salt, and pepper.
Heat a pan over medium-high heat. Cook chicken cubes for 6-8 minutes, turning occasionally, until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 75°C. Set aside to cool slightly.
Dice tomatoes and cucumber into 1.5 cm cubes. Thinly slice red onion. Halve Kalamata olives.
Crumble feta cheese into small pieces.
For the dressing, whisk together remaining olive oil, red wine vinegar, 1 clove minced garlic, salt, and pepper in a small bowl.
In a large serving bowl, combine diced tomatoes, cucumber, red onion, Kalamata olives, and crumbled feta. Add the cooled grilled chicken cubes.
Pour dressing over the salad. Gently toss to combine all ingredients.
Roughly chop fresh basil and remaining fresh oregano. Sprinkle over the salad just before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Herb Chicken
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. A single, golden-brown seared chicken thigh, bone-in and skin-on, is positioned centrally. The chicken is nestled in a rich, rustic red braised tomato sauce, which features visible chunks of diced red bell pepper and halved Kalamata olives. The sauce has a glossy, thick texture. Bright green fresh basil leaves are scattered generously over the chicken and sauce, providing a fresh contrast. A subtle drizzle of olive oil glistens on the surface. The background features a simple light wooden table surface and a folded off-white cotton napkin beside the plate. The scene is lit with soft, natural, even lighting, creating a warm, inviting ambiance. The chicken is whole, not sliced. The plate is not overcrowded, allowing for moderate negative space. A small, rustic piece of crusty bread is placed to the side of the plate.
instructions: Pat chicken dry. Season chicken generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large braising pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down until deeply golden brown, about 5-7 minutes. Flip chicken. Sear other side for 3-4 minutes. Remove chicken from pan. Set aside.
Add diced onion and diced bell pepper to the hot pan. Sauté for 5 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic to the pan. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in crushed tomatoes and chicken broth. Stir in dried oregano and dried basil. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared chicken to the pan, skin-side up. Add halved Kalamata olives around the chicken.
Reduce heat to low. Cover the pan. Simmer gently for 30-40 minutes, or until chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F) and is very tender.
Taste the sauce. Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper if needed.
Garnish generously with fresh chopped basil before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Cherry & Peanut Butter Chocolate Bark
recipes.visual_description: The Fermented Cherry & Peanut Butter Chocolate Bark is presented on a light, natural-textured reclaimed wood board. Irregular, thick chunks of dark chocolate bark are arranged casually across the surface, showcasing their organic breaks. The deep, glossy brown of the dark chocolate base is marbled with swirls of creamy, lighter brown peanut butter. Scattered across the surface are vibrant, plump fermented cherry halves, their reddish-purple hues providing bright contrast. Some cherry pieces are fully embedded, while others protrude slightly, revealing their soft, preserved texture. A very light dusting of white icing sugar, almost imperceptible, adds a subtle frosty finish to some pieces. The overall composition is clean and minimalist, with ample negative space. The handcrafted ceramic plate in an earthy cream tone, visible beneath the board, complements the natural aesthetic. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the scene, enhancing the textures and colors of the ingredients. A simple, undyed linen napkin in natural beige is casually draped nearby. The background is clean and unobtrusive, with hints of green foliage from a potted plant, reinforcing the eco-conscious theme.
instructions: Prepare fermentation brine: Dissolve sea salt in non-chlorinated water. Stir until clear.
Place pitted cherries into a clean, sterile jar. Pour brine over cherries, ensuring they are fully submerged. Leave 2 cm headspace.
Seal jar loosely to allow gas release. Ferment at room temperature (20-24°C) for 3-5 days. Burp daily. Taste for desired tanginess. Refrigerate once fermented.
Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Melt dark chocolate using a double boiler or microwave. Stir until smooth.
Pour melted chocolate onto parchment paper. Spread thinly and evenly into a rectangle (approx. 20x25 cm).
Warm peanut butter slightly for easier drizzling. Drizzle peanut butter over the chocolate. Use a skewer to swirl gently for a marbled effect.
Remove fermented cherries from brine. Pat dry. Scatter cherries evenly over the chocolate and peanut butter mixture.
Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or until chocolate is completely set and firm.
Break the hardened bark into irregular, rustic pieces. Lightly dust with icing sugar if desired. Serve immediately or store in an airtight container in the refrigerator.

recipes.recipe_name: Bell Pepper and Roasted Chicken Salad
recipes.visual_description: The Bell Pepper and Roasted Chicken Salad is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, showcasing a vibrant array of colors and textures. Roasted red and yellow bell pepper wedges, caramelized red onion slices, and tender roasted zucchini chunks are artfully arranged over a bed of fresh, crisp mixed greens. Small, bite-sized pieces of roasted chicken breast are interspersed among the vegetables. Bright, whole cherry tomatoes add pops of red. A light balsamic vinaigrette coats the greens and components. The overall composition is balanced, allowing for moderate negative space. The dish is set on a simple wooden table, accompanied by standard flatware and a cotton napkin, under natural, even lighting, evoking a modern bistro atmosphere.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (390°F). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Cut bell peppers into 2 cm wedges. Cut red onion into 1 cm slices. Cut zucchini into 2 cm chunks. Halve garlic cloves.
Toss bell peppers, red onion, garlic, cherry tomatoes, and zucchini with 30 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper on the baking sheet.
Place chicken breasts on the same baking sheet, seasoning with salt and pepper.
Roast for 20-25 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and vegetables are tender-crisp.
Remove chicken from oven. Let rest 5 minutes, then dice into 2 cm pieces.
While chicken rests, prepare the dressing. In a small bowl, whisk together remaining 30 ml olive oil, balsamic vinegar, Dijon mustard, and honey. Season with salt and pepper.
In a large bowl, combine roasted vegetables, diced chicken, and mixed greens. Drizzle with dressing.
Toss gently to combine all ingredients.
Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure chicken is cooked to a minimum internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
For an extra touch, reduce a small amount of balsamic vinegar separately to create a thicker balsamic glaze for drizzling over the finished salad.

recipes.recipe_name: Sweet Potato & Kale Salad with Tahini Dressing
recipes.visual_description: The salad is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, showcasing a harmonious blend of colors and textures. Roasted sweet potato cubes, exhibiting a warm, earthy orange hue with slightly caramelized edges, are interspersed with vibrant, dark green sautéed kale leaves. Thinly sliced ruby-red red onion rings add a contrasting pop of color. A creamy, pale tan tahini dressing is artfully drizzled over the components, binding them together. Chopped toasted pecans are scattered generously on top, providing a textural crunch. The arrangement is professional yet approachable, with moderate negative space on the plate. The entire plate is visible, placed on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the fresh ingredients and inviting presentation.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Toss diced sweet potatoes with 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Roast for 20-25 minutes, or until tender and lightly caramelized. Let cool slightly.

Heat 15ml olive oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add minced garlic and sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant. Add chopped kale and sauté for 3-5 minutes until wilted. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside.

In a small bowl, whisk together tahini, lemon juice, maple syrup, Dijon mustard, 30ml olive oil, and 30ml water until smooth. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Adjust consistency with more water if needed.
In a large bowl, combine roasted sweet potatoes, sautéed kale, and thinly sliced red onion. Pour the tahini dressing over the salad. Toss gently to coat all ingredients evenly.
Divide the salad among four plates. Garnish each serving with chopped toasted pecans. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Pork and Vegetable Madras Curry
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Creamy Pork and Vegetable Madras Curry is presented in a clean, white, shallow porcelain bowl, on a simple wooden table. The rich, golden-brown curry features tender pork chunks (2-3 cm cubes) coated in creamy sauce. Diced carrots and green peas provide vibrant orange and green accents. Shredded cabbage adds textural contrast. Fresh, chopped green coriander leaves garnish the top. The sauce has a moderate, free-flowing consistency. A simple cotton napkin is folded beside the bowl. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's warmth and inviting colors. The background is subtly blurred, suggesting a casual restaurant atmosphere, allowing the dish to remain the clear focal point.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with plain basmati rice or naan bread on the side.
Offer a simple raita (yogurt dip) or cucumber salad as a cooling accompaniment.
instructions: Pat pork cubes dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Brown pork cubes in batches. Remove pork and set aside.
Add diced onion to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and diced carrot. Cook for 3 minutes, stirring.
Stir in madras curry powder. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Return browned pork to the pot. Add diced tomato, pork stock, soy sauce, and Dijon mustard (if using).
Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 45-60 minutes, or until pork is tender.
Add shredded cabbage and green peas. Cook for another 10-15 minutes, or until vegetables are tender-crisp.
Stir in heavy cream. Simmer gently for 5 minutes, do not boil.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Garnish with fresh coriander before serving.
notes: For deeper flavor, marinate pork cubes in a little curry powder and yogurt for an hour before cooking.
Adjust spice level by increasing or decreasing madras curry powder.
This dish pairs well with a light lager or a crisp white wine.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Beef and Potato Lentil Stew
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of hearty beef and potato lentil stew is presented in an everyday ceramic bowl, deep and slightly irregular, resting on a well-used wooden dining table. The stew is rich with tender, rustic chunks of braised beef, soft brown lentils, and diced potatoes, all suspended in a thick, savory tomato-based broth. Diced onions are visible, adding depth. The colors are earthy browns, deep reds from the tomato, and the light yellow of potatoes, with a scattering of fresh green chopped parsley on top. The textures are comforting and varied: the melt-in-your-mouth beef contrasts with the creamy lentils and tender potato cubes. The stew fills the bowl naturally, its components touching and overlapping in a casual, home-style arrangement. A simple metal spoon rests beside the bowl on a casually placed cloth napkin. Warm, natural light illuminates the scene, suggesting a cozy family kitchen setting.

ingredients.name: Beef chuck, diced into 2.5 cm chunks
Potatoes, peeled and diced into 2 cm cubes

instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add beef chunks. Sear until browned on all sides. Remove beef from pot.
Add diced onions to the pot. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and cayenne pepper. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Return beef to the pot. Add rinsed lentils, diced potatoes, diced tomatoes, chicken stock, dried thyme, and bay leaf.
Bring the stew to a boil. Reduce heat to low.
Cover and simmer for 1.5 to 2 hours. Stew is ready when beef is very tender and lentils are soft.
Remove bay leaf.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Ladle hot stew into bowls. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Chicken Breast with Creamy Madras Cabbage and Tomato
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Seared Chicken Breast with Creamy Madras Cabbage and Tomato is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, set on a simple wooden table. The seared chicken breast, displaying a golden-brown crust, is either served whole or sliced into thick medallions, placed atop or alongside a generous mound of the creamy cabbage. The braised cabbage, coarsely shredded, retains a vibrant green hue, coated in a rich, orange-red madras curry and tomato sauce. The sauce is smooth, clinging to the cabbage, showcasing its creamy texture. Fresh, bright green coriander leaves are scattered over the dish as a garnish, providing a color contrast. The arrangement is professional yet approachable, with moderate negative space. Standard flatware and a folded cotton napkin complete the modern bistro setting under natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Steamed basmati rice
Warm naan bread
instructions: Prepare chicken: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Sear chicken: Heat 15ml oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breasts 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown. Internal temperature should reach 75°C. Remove chicken. Set aside.
Sauté aromatics: Add remaining oil to the pan. Add diced onion. Sauté 5 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic and grated ginger. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Add spices and tomato: Stir in madras curry powder. Cook 1 minute, stirring constantly. Add chopped tomatoes and chicken stock. Bring to a simmer.
Braise cabbage: Add coarsely shredded cabbage to the pan. Stir to combine. Cover. Simmer 15-20 minutes until cabbage is tender.
Finish sauce: Stir in double cream and soy sauce. Simmer 5 minutes until sauce slightly thickens. Season with salt and pepper.
Serve: Slice chicken breasts into thick medallions or serve whole. Plate creamy madras cabbage. Place chicken on top or beside the cabbage. Garnish with fresh coriander.

recipes.recipe_name: Lentil Potato Stew with Pickled Onion
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of hearty lentil and potato stew is presented in a handcrafted, unglazed ceramic bowl with a natural, earthy tone. The stew is rich and fluid, showcasing the tender, distinct brown lentils and soft 2cm potato cubes. A vibrant pop of color comes from a generous spoonful of bright pink pickled onion slices, artfully placed atop the stew.
